author_or_account: Thomas Akana / Federal Reserve Bank of Philadelphia
title: Are Household Perceptions of Borrowing Costs Creating Spending Headwinds?
discussion_signal: The Philadelphia Fed relay describes the July 2026 Consumer Finance Institute survey of more than 4,000 adults. It reports that over one-quarter considered borrowing for a large purchase but did not proceed, with about half of that group citing high borrowing costs; about 5% instead purchased a less ideal version because financing was expensive. This is direct survey evidence of substitution and forgone purchases, while the post does not identify every product category or establish a causal experiment.
linked_research_question: Which household groups and purchase categories lose access first when perceived borrowing costs rise, and do cheaper substitutes preserve welfare or reduce product quality?
limits: The post summarizes survey responses and does not provide a randomized causal estimate
The reported shares do not reveal the distribution across income, credit score, product type, or region
A less ideal purchase is self-reported and does not measure long-run welfare or repayment outcomes
